name: Sumau
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Only Z'graggen Madang wordlists/classification; no stress description located.

sources.citation: OLAC: resources in and about the Sumau language [six] (language-archives.org, as of 2025-11-04)
sources.note: Catalog only: lists Rosetta Swadesh list, transnewguinea.org, Glottolog, Ethnologue, LINGUIST List and Z'graggen 1980; no SIL or other descriptive item for Sumau.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J.A. 1971. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Madang District. Pacific Linguistics C-19. Canberra: ANU. viii+179 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: p.6: 'The marking of stress has been omitted, since the stress patterning has not been well established yet.' Sec. 2.21.2-2.21.23 (pp.36-38) Usur Group incl. Sumau (Garia): 12 typological features, none prosodic.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J.A. 1980. A comparative word list of the Rai Coast languages, Madang Province, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics D-30. Canberra: ANU. xvi+196 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Intro sec. 7 (pp. vii-viii): transcription 'rendered in a semiphonemic form'; lists sound fluctuations for Sumau (B15); no mention of stress or accent anywhere in the volume (a full-text search for stress/accent + read of intro). Sumau forms carry length marks but no stress marks.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, Johannes A. 1975. The Madang-Adelbert Range Sub-Phylum. In S.A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea Area Languages and Language Study Vol 1, Pacific Linguistics C-38:569-612.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 2.8.2.2.1.1.4 Peka Family (Usino, Sumau, Urigina, Danaru): classification only; no phonology, no stress.

sources.citation: Claassen, Oren R. & McElhanon, Kenneth A. 1970. Languages of the Finisterre Range. Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 11, Pacific Linguistics A-23:45-78.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 3.1 Usino Family (pp.58-59): Garia (Sumau) classification, lexicostatistics and population only; nothing on stress for Garia (the only stress remark in the paper concerns a Finisterre language, citing Davis 1967).

sources.citation: Z'graggen, John A. 1969. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Madang District, New Guinea. PhD thesis, Australian National University. x+335 pp. (hdl 1885/130077)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Explicitly silent: Part One pp.13-14 (pdf p.22) 'The marking of stress has been omitted, since the stress patterning has not been well established yet.' Usur Group (Usino, Sumau, Urigina) typological features are segmental only (glottal stop present only in Sumau).

sources.note: Z'graggen recorded Sumau but withheld stress marking in print; raw field transcriptions or audio would be the only primary evidence of Sumau stress.
